verification.method: scripts/verify/labour-112.py reads the original World Bank zips (data/raw/wdi/), not the site's generated data; check-wdi.mjs compares all generated WDI values with the original files; then the text was read by hand
verification.what: every ranking row (182 countries and areas, order and value), the men's rate and gap columns, the CSV, every figure in the text, FAQ, title, description and JSON-LD; claims: world 48.9% for women and 73.1% for men in 2025, 51.1% in 1991 and lowest in 2020, Madagascar, Solomon Islands, Nigeria highest and Yemen, Afghanistan, Iraq lowest, all ten countries below 20% in the Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan and Pakistan region, women ahead of men only in Burundi and Moldova, Bangladesh 38.6% (152nd) from 24.6% in 1991, Saudi Arabia 2.3-fold since 1991; definition from the indicator notes
verification.against: World Bank WDI bulk files and indicator metadata (update 11 November 2026, CC BY 4.0; ILO modelled estimates)
verification.result: All automated comparisons matched; a sentence about unpaid work at home was removed before publishing because the World Bank notes do not state it

changelog.note: First version: ILO modelled labour force participation of women and men via World Bank WDI, 2025.
